$comment: SHARED CONTRACT — band arithmetic for map_split_registry.bands (M2.6).
Both sides derive the same quantities from the same stored blob, so both sides must
read it identically. This file is the specification; server and client are each
checked AGAINST it rather than against each other.
Consumers:
server  -> server/tests/test_transfer_plan.py (must pass; part of the pytest suite)
client  -> contracts/band_arithmetic/client_harness.mjs (read-only; reports divergence)
WHY `to_cases` IS SHORT, AND WHY IT MUST STAY SHORT (2026-07-27).
It is tempting to grow this into a coercion table. Do not. The WRITE PATH is
constrained, so most of that table would pin agreement on values that cannot be
stored:
* the panel's end-layer field is <input type=number min=1 step=1>
(transfer_plan.js), and its change handler runs the typed text through the same
classifier and REFUSES anything invalid - it never reaches storage;
* normalizeBands/serializeBands (map_editor.js) write `to` as a number for ok and
'' for blank -- but an INVALID value is preserved VERBATIM (map_editor.js:230),
deliberately: blanking it would destroy the panel's only evidence that the value
is wrong, and it would then compute as 0 layers with nobody the wiser.
So the panel cannot ORIGINATE '0x10', '1_0', '1e3', true, [] or an out-of-range
magnitude -- but it faithfully PRESERVES one the grid created, so such a value can
survive a round trip. The only writer that creates them is the generic data grid,
and for that the server
needs ONE rule, not a mirror: anything it cannot read as an integer is `invalid` ->
layer_range_invalid -> unverified. That rule does not need to match the client's
coercion, because the client will never have produced such a value. Enumerating more
of that class buys agreement on garbage and costs a table nobody can keep true.
So this group covers exactly: the two blank spellings a real row can hold, the happy
path, and ONE representative of the unreadable class per branch of the rule.
The behavioural rules live elsewhere and are the part with teeth:
* sequence_cases       - the derivation itself (prev_to / layers / total / share)
* invalid_between_...  - blank and invalid are skipped identically by the walk
* normalize_roundtrip  - derived in the harness; guards the WRITER, which is where
the constraint lives. It caught normalizeBands storing 16
for '0x10' - the highest-value defect this file has found.
NaN / Infinity are absent on purpose: JSON cannot express them, so they are not
reachable through the stored column. The server covers them in a unit test.
to states:  blank = not decided yet (0 layers, not an error)
ok    = finite JSON number, or trimmed decimal-integer string, |v| <= 2^53
invalid = everything else

to_cases.$comment: Five cases, one per decision. Read the WHY note at the top of this file before adding a sixth - the write path is constrained and this axis is about degradation, not parity.

to_cases.name: null
to_cases.$why: What serializeBands actually writes for an unfinished band. Blank is not 0 - that distinction is the whole reason for a tri-state.

to_cases.name: absent_key
to_cases.$why: A row written before `to` existed, or a hand-built one. Same answer as null.

to_cases.name: empty_string
to_cases.$why: Legacy rows hold '' where new writes hold null.

to_cases.name: int
to_cases.$why: The happy path - the only shape the panel can store.

to_cases.name: unreadable
to_cases.$why: ONE representative of the whole unreadable class (grid-written text). The server's rule is single: not readable as an integer -> invalid -> layer_range_invalid -> unverified. It does NOT need to agree with the client's coercion, because the client cannot have produced this. Do not re-enumerate '0x10' / '1_0' / '1e3' / true / [] here - they all take this same branch, and sequence_cases already pins that an invalid band is skipped by the walk exactly like a blank one.

to_cases.name: over_max_layer
to_cases.$why: KEPT DELIBERATELY, and it is not a coercion case. This is the second branch of the rule: readable as an integer but out of range. It guards a server-side consequence that exists no matter who wrote the value - `to` feeds painted x layers, so an unbounded magnitude puts a 301-digit integer into `required` in the response. Deleting this vector would let the MAX_LAYER bound be removed with the suite still green. Stated as a decimal string so both sides parse it exactly (a JSON number past 2^53 is rounded by JSON.parse before any guard runs).

sequence_cases.name: blank_between_does_not_reset_the_walk
sequence_cases.$why: The divergence that motivated this file. A whitespace `to` reads as 0 under JS coercion, which STOPS the backward walk; under this spec it is blank and is SKIPPED. One screen, two numbers for the same material.

sequence_cases.name: invalid_between_is_skipped_exactly_like_blank
sequence_cases.$why: The structural rule. If invalid stopped the walk at 0 while blank skipped it, every coercion quirk would become its own divergence.

sequence_cases.name: non_increasing_inflates_the_next_band
sequence_cases.$why: A reversed `to` does NOT stop the walk - it is a valid number. The empty band contributes nothing, but the band after it counts from the low value, so the stack over-counts. 10 + 15 = 25 layers for a 20-layer stack.

sequence_cases.name: array_position_is_order_seq_is_only_identity
sequence_cases.$why: Sorting by seq would flip the layer counts and drag materials into the wrong band.

sequence_cases.name: share_rounds_up
sequence_cases.$why: Floor or round would hide a shortage.

sequence_cases.name: painted_scales_the_total
sequence_cases.$why: Nothing derived is stored - painting one more cell must move the demand.

normalization_cases.name: duplicate_seq_is_resolved_not_merged
normalization_cases.$why: seq used to be part of a composite business key, so collisions were impossible. It now arrives in a browser-written JSON blob through a plain varchar column. Two bands sharing a seq must stay two bands.

normalization_cases.name: missing_seq_falls_back_to_position
normalization_cases.$why: Position fallback gives band 0 seq 1; band 1 already declares 2. No collision, nothing to resolve. Contrast with the next case.

normalization_cases.name: position_fallback_can_collide_and_must_be_resolved
normalization_cases.$why: Band 1 has no seq, so position fallback proposes 2 - which band 0 already holds. Unresolved, both label as #2 and the over-allocation guard sees one demand instead of two.

normalization_cases.name: non_object_element_is_dropped_not_fatal
normalization_cases.$why: One bad element must not void the whole value's plan.

normalization_cases.name: invalid_seq_types_fall_back_to_position
normalization_cases.$why: ONE case for the whole seq type axis, same reasoning as to_cases: normalizeBands assigns an integer seq, so a non-integer seq is grid-only. The rule is single - not a positive integer means fall back to array position - and it does not need to agree with the client's coercion on values the panel cannot write. Do not expand this into a type table.

materials_cases.$comment: Behavioural rules that BOTH sides agree on and the panel can actually produce. Empty-dropping and dedupe belong here because they change len(materials), which is the divisor in share = ceil(total / len(materials)) - a derived number, not a formatting detail. This group is deliberately NOT an element-type table: a non-string element is grid-only, and the server REFUSES it (source_unresolved -> unverified) rather than stringifying it. There is nothing to be consistent with, because the panel writes materials through a text input and has never produced a number, a bool or an object. Do not add vectors trying to make the two sides stringify garbage the same way - the server-side refusal is covered by pytest, where it belongs.

material_split_cases.$comment: Rule: plan_store.material_identity {compose:[lot,slot], separator:'_'}. Split from the RIGHT so the FIRST field absorbs extras. Refuse rather than guess - a material that does not resolve must not be reported as availability 0.
